summary:
The Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 temporarily suspends the federal debt limit and establishes budgetary and policy changes related to federal spending, rescissions, benefit programs, student loans, permitting, and energy infrastructure.

The Act amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 to set discretionary spending limits for fiscal years 2024 and 2025: $886.349 billion and $895.212 billion for the revised security category, and $703.651 billion and $710.688 billion for the revised nonsecurity category. It also provides specified cap adjustments for disability reviews, health care fraud control, disaster funding, and reemployment services, and sets additional discretionary spending limits for fiscal years 2026 through 2029 for budget enforcement purposes. If any continuing appropriations are in effect on or after January 1 of fiscal year 2024 or 2025, the Act provides for revised limits based on fiscal year 2023 base funding reduced by 1 percent, unless full-year appropriations are enacted. It also appropriates funds for the Cost of War Toxic Exposures Fund and the Department of Commerce Nonrecurring Expenses Fund.

The Act establishes temporary House and Senate budget enforcement procedures for fiscal years 2024 and 2025, including limits on advance appropriations with specified exceptions. It permanently rescinds numerous unobligated balances from prior appropriations, including COVID-19-related funds, and rescinds $1.389525 billion from certain Internal Revenue Service funds made available by the Inflation Reduction Act.

The Act creates the Administrative Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2023, requiring certain agency rules that increase direct spending to be offset by other administrative actions reducing direct spending, subject to exemptions, waivers, no judicial review, a GAO report, and expiration on December 31, 2024.

It ends the federal student loan payment suspension and interest waiver 60 days after June 30, 2023, and bars further extensions except by later Act of Congress. It modifies TANF work-related rules and reporting, generally effective October 1, 2024, with some provisions effective October 1, 2025. It changes SNAP work requirement exemptions, including age thresholds and exemptions for homeless individuals, veterans, and certain former foster youth, with those changes sunsetting October 1, 2030.

The Act amends NEPA review procedures, deadlines, page limits, lead agency rules, categorical exclusions, and related definitions; requires an interregional electric transfer capability study; adds energy storage to FAST Act covered sectors; and ratifies and directs completion-related approvals for the Mountain Valley Pipeline. It suspends the debt limit through January 1, 2025, with the limit increased on January 2, 2025, to reflect necessary obligations issued during the suspension period.
